harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured PostgreSQL 13 streaming replication across the RHEL 9 cluster: node1 is the writable primary, node2 and node3 are read-only async standbys built via pg_basebackup with generated SCRAM credentials. Verified writes on the primary propagate to both standbys and standbys reject writes. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol (standbys first, primary last) with changed boot-time proof and confirmed full replication recovery and data continuity after each restart.
actions_performed: Installed postgresql-server/contrib on node1, node2, node3 (RHEL 9 AppStream, PG 13.23)
Initialized DB on node1, configured wal_level=replica, max_wal_senders, hot_standby, listen_addresses='*' and password_encryption=[REDACTED]
Opened firewalld postgresql service on all three nodes
Added pg_hba.conf rules for replication and client access from the cluster subnet
Created 'replicator' role on node1 with a node-generated random password (fixed initial md5-vs-scram mismatch by setting password_encryption before storing the password)
Set up passwordless SSH between nodes using the cluster-provided keypair solely to transfer the replication password file securely to node2/node3 (deleted after use)
Ran pg_basebackup -R -X stream on node2 and node3 to clone node1 and auto-generate standby.signal + primary_conninfo
Started postgresql on all nodes; verified pg_stat_replication shows both standbys streaming and pg_is_in_recovery()=true on standbys
Created repl_test table, inserted a row on primary, confirmed visibility on both standbys, and confirmed standbys reject INSERT (read-only)
Captured pre-restart baseline (machine-id, uptime -s boot time, replication/data state) on all nodes

Rebooted node2, then node3, then node1 (primary) one at a time via native reboot, polling exec availability, confirming machine-id unchanged but uptime -s (boot time) changed, and reverifying postgresql active + replication streaming + data intact after each
Performed a final post-restart write on node1 and confirmed it replicated to node2 and node3

evidence.requirement: node1 configured as writable primary with replication enabled
evidence.summary: postgresql-server initialized, wal_level/hot_standby/pg_hba configured, service started, replicator role created with working SCRAM password

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 configured as read-only standbys via streaming replication from node1
evidence.summary: pg_basebackup -R -X stream completed on both nodes generating standby.signal/primary_conninfo; postgresql service started successfully

evidence.requirement: Standbys are streaming and in read-only recovery mode
evidence.summary: pg_stat_replication on primary shows both nodes 'streaming'; pg_is_in_recovery() returns true on node2 and node3

evidence.requirement: Changes committed on the primary are visible on both standbys
evidence.summary: Row inserted on node1 immediately visible via SELECT on node2 and node3; standbys also proven read-only by rejecting INSERT

evidence.requirement: Healthy baseline captured before any restart
evidence.summary: Captured machine-id, uptime -s boot time, and repl_test row count on all three nodes prior to restarts

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; machine-id unchanged but uptime -s changed from 21:17:26 to 21:21:29; postgresql active, still in recovery, data intact, reconnected as streaming standby on primary

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: reboot acknowledged; machine-id unchanged but uptime -s changed from 21:17:26 to 21:21:48; postgresql active, in recovery, data intact, reconnected as streaming standby

evidence.requirement: node1 (primary) restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state, cluster fully healed
evidence.summary: reboot acknowledged; machine-id unchanged but uptime -s changed from 21:17:26 to 21:22:09; postgresql active, both standbys reconnected as streaming within seconds; final post-restart write on node1 replicated to both node2 and node3, confirming complete cluster health
